name: Tia-Clair Toomey
who: Most decorated athlete in CrossFit Games history, 8-time Fittest Woman on Earth through the 2025 season.
why: Sets the competitive standard the entire women's field trains against; her app and gear line extend that authority into commerce.

name: Mat Fraser
who: Five-time CrossFit Games champion (2016-2020), widely regarded as the greatest individual competitor in the sport's history.
why: Retired unbeaten in Games finals; his name still headlines comeback speculation and his training company keeps his standards visible.

name: Rich Froning
who: Four-time individual CrossFit Games champion and multi-time team champion, founder of CrossFit Mayhem.
why: Built the sport's biggest affiliate-and-media brand and still competes and coaches team events, bridging the sport's early and current eras.

name: Katrin Davidsdottir
who: Two-time Fittest Woman on Earth (2015, 2016) and veteran competitor still contending for the Games podium.
why: A decade-plus at the top with a large, loyal following and co-founded nutrition and recovery brands.

name: Annie Thorisdottir
who: First two-time Fittest Woman on Earth (2011, 2012), one of the sport's founding stars.
why: Her early dominance helped put women's CrossFit on equal billing with the men's field; still a respected voice and occasional competitor.

name: Sara Sigmundsdottir
who: Longtime individual Games competitor and Mayhem Freedom team athlete known for raw strength and candid, personality-driven content.
why: One of the more entertaining, outspoken voices in the sport, with a following that predates and outlasts her competitive peak.

name: James Sprague
who: Two-time Fittest Man on Earth (2024, 2026), the current standard-bearer of the men's field.
why: Fresh off defending his title, he is the sport's newest breakout star, with reach still catching up to his results.

name: Aimee Cringle
who: 2026 Fittest Woman on Earth, the first British Games champion since Sam Briggs in 2013.
why: A six-year rise from mid-pack to champion that is reshaping the UK CrossFit scene and drawing new mainstream press.

name: Dallin Pepper
who: Multiple-time CrossFit Games podium finisher, runner-up in 2026, long tipped as the next Fittest Man on Earth.
why: A young, telegenic contender whose near-misses have made him one of the most-discussed men in the sport.

name: Emma Lawson
who: Runner-up at the 2026 CrossFit Games and one of the sport's most consistent young podium threats.
why: Canada's top current CrossFit export, with a fast-growing following tracking her rise toward a title.

name: Justin Medeiros
who: Two-time Fittest Man on Earth (2021, 2022) and one of the most consistently ranked men of the past five years.
why: A crossover face for the sport with strong brand deals and steady top-5 Games finishes since his titles.

name: Jeffrey Adler
who: 2023 Fittest Man on Earth and back-to-back Rogue Invitational champion (2024, 2025).
why: Canada's most decorated current male competitor, still adding to a growing trophy case.

name: Laura Horvath
who: 2023 Fittest Woman on Earth, Hungary's first CrossFit Games champion.
why: Broke a long US/Icelandic/Australian hold on the women's title and remains a top podium threat.

name: Brooke Wells
who: Longtime individual Games competitor and one of the most consistent top-10 women of the past decade.
why: A steady top finisher with strong sponsor relationships and a loyal training-content following.

name: Danielle Brandon
who: Multiple-time CrossFit Games individual competitor known for explosive gymnastics and a fast-growing profile.
why: One of the more talked-about rising women in the sport, with viral-friendly training clips.

name: Noah Ohlsen
who: Ten-plus-year individual Games competitor, among the most durable men's careers in the sport.
why: Rarely misses a Games appearance and is respected as one of the field's most consistent performers.

name: Kristi Eramo O'Connell
who: Multiple-time individual Games competitor and coach known for technical lifting content.
why: A steady presence bridging elite competition and everyday training advice for a broad training audience.

name: Chandler Smith
who: Individual Games competitor and one of the sport's strongest young men, known for elite weightlifting numbers.
why: A rising name whose raw strength numbers get shared well outside the CrossFit community.

name: Hunter McIntyre
who: Three-time HYROX World Champion and founder of BLDR Sports, formerly a top obstacle-course/Spartan racer.
why: The loudest, most recognizable face driving HYROX's US growth, with a hybrid-training persona built for virality.

name: Alexander Roncevic
who: Austrian HYROX World Champion and double world-record holder, first athlete to break the 52-minute barrier.
why: The technical benchmark of the sport right now, setting times and standards other elite racers chase.

name: Lauren Weeks
who: Three-time HYROX World Champion, the most decorated woman in the sport.
why: The benchmark competitor for women's HYROX as the sport professionalizes and its audience grows.

name: Megan Jacoby
who: 2024 HYROX World Champion and one of the sport's top-ranked women.
why: A recent breakout champion helping legitimize HYROX as a pro women's circuit.

name: Marston Sawyers
who: Co-founder of the Buttery Bros, CrossFit's best-known documentary and comedy media duo (with Heber Cannon).
why: Their films and event coverage have shaped how the whole sport is presented on camera, and their apparel brand extends that reach.

name: Ben Bergeron
who: Founder of CompTrain and CrossFit New England, coach behind multiple individual and team Games champions.
why: The sport's most influential coach: his programming and mindset content are studied and copied across affiliates worldwide.

name: Marcus Filly
who: Former CrossFit Games competitor turned founder of Functional Bodybuilding, a training style he popularized.
why: Created and named a training category now used across gyms worldwide, backed by a real subscription-program business.

name: Craig Richey
who: British Weightlifting national champion turned YouTube fitness personality, known for daily follow-along cardio and CrossFit-style content.
why: One of the sport's longest-running creators, translating CrossFit and weightlifting training into daily content for a mainstream audience.
